. Carmack, a veteran computer programmer and video game designer, argued in a detailed post on X that AI is making traditional hand-coding skills potentially obsolete.

He explained his point by comparing the development of AI with the way martial arts changed after World War II. Martial arts originally developed as a way to survive and fight on the battlefield, but later became a sport and a form of personal discipline.

He wrote, “AI is making many other programming skills much less critical. We aren’t there yet, but carefully writing code completely by hand is moving from a -jitsu to a -do. Code-do? Codo?” In martial arts terminology, “-jitsu” refers to techniques focused on combat, while “-do” refers to a practice focused on personal development. Carmack used this distinction to suggest manual coding may be shifting from a survival skill programmers need for their work to a specialized craft they practice by choice.
He also added that programmers should avoid becoming “the out of touch Kung Fu master… that gets mauled by an amateur MMA fighter.”
